A1.justification: Both 18-page PDFs describe DreamShot and contain corresponding main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–C. Text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A–B report original benchmark evaluations, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and generated storyboard examples.

after.justification: The original DreamShot evaluations and supplementary experimental results remain in Section 5 and Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same video-VAE/DiT framework, shot-wise cross-attention, three generation modes, Role-Attention Consistency Loss, and reference-free guidance. Text crossing page boundaries is reflowed, without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same real and synthetic storyboard data and evaluate on the DreamShot Test Set and VistoryBench. Generation tasks and supplementary long-sequence, motion, and storyboard-to-video scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator membership within each generation mode. Table 2 retains Story-Adapter, SEED-Story, UNO, OmniGen2, and QwenImage; qualitative comparator participation is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains Wan2.1-14B, 10k training iterations at 192p followed by 10k at 480p, the same evaluation metrics, and the same benchmark sizes: 100 DreamShot samples and 80 VistoryBench stories. Supplementary experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The RACL, reference-position, guidance-weight, and LoRA-rank ablations remain unchanged. Appendices retain the same data-source comparisons, loss-weight sensitivity, sequence-length analysis, qualitative examples, and motion failure cases.

E5.justification: Tables 1–4 and the analysis plots retain the same statistical presentation. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative examples are unchanged, including the appendices. For example, DreamShot's reference-to-shot CIDS Self/Cross scores remain 48.7/51.6 in Table 1, and its CIDS-Cross score remains 60.2 in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9), including the attention definitions, flow-matching objective, RACL, and guidance formulation, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about video diffusion priors, personalized storyboard generation, RACL, the constructed dataset, and improved consistency and generation efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the ablations and data-source comparisons are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same limitations concerning extremely long storyboards, weak motion cues caused by frame filtering, and output resolution.

D1.justification: Implementation and preprocessing disclosures are unchanged, including AdamW, learning rate 3×10^-5, LoRA rank 256, guidance weights, eight A800 GPUs, approximately 48 hours of training, and Appendix A.1's data-processing steps. The project link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 60 references and related-work discussion remain. Positioning against image-based storyboard generation, personalization methods, and video-generation approaches is unchanged.

P1.justification: The author block removes Peng Cheng Laboratory and Guangdong Key Laboratory of Big Data Analysis and Processing, with corresponding affiliation-superscript changes. The arXiv version/date header is updated; substantive prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The shorter affiliation block shifts Figure 1 and surrounding text upward and causes limited column and page-break reflow across pages 1–4. Figure and table content and captions are unchanged; pages 5–18 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 updates affiliations and slightly reflows the opening pages. Methods, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, claims, and limitations—including the appendices—remain unchanged. These administrative and layout edits establish no meaningful net improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
